To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum levels of NO are significantly lower in obese children than in normal children.
the serum levels of nitric oxide are significantly lower in overweight and obese children, compared with normal-weight children.
the serum level of nitrite/nitrate, the end products of NO synthesis, was significantly lower in obese children than in healthy children.
